tricky_patterns.description: Uses Reflection to dynamically invoke methods by name: typeof(PowerView).GetMethod(methodName).Invoke()
tricky_patterns.c_sharp_code: var method = typeof(PowerView).GetMethod(methodName); var ret = method.Invoke(null, new[] { argObject });
tricky_patterns.mitigation: Replace with compile-time code generation using procedural macros or match statement mapping method names to functions
tricky_patterns.rust_strategy: Use clap derive macro for CLI parsing; dispatch via match statement or inventory crate for registration pattern

tricky_patterns.description: TypeDescriptor.GetConverter() for runtime type conversion from strings to arbitrary types
tricky_patterns.mitigation: Use FromStr trait and match/dispatch based on expected types; clap handles this automatically
tricky_patterns.rust_strategy: Leverage clap's automatic string→type conversion via FromStr trait implementations

tricky_patterns.description: 28 DllImport declarations with complex marshalling: IntPtr, out params, StructLayout, MarshalAs attributes
tricky_patterns.mitigation: Use windows crate for type-safe bindings; wrap unsafe calls in safe abstractions with RAII cleanup
tricky_patterns.rust_strategy: 1) Prefer windows::Win32::* bindings over manual declarations. 2) Wrap in safe functions that handle encoding (UTF-16), memory management (NetApiBufferFree), and error handling. 3) Use ManuallyDrop/MaybeUninit for out params

examples.issue: Caller must free returned buffer with NetApiBufferFree
examples.rust_pattern: RAII wrapper struct that calls NetApiBufferFree in Drop

examples.issue: Returns token handle that must be closed; password in plaintext
examples.rust_pattern: Return HandleGuard that CloseHandle on drop; use secrecy::SecretString for password
Zero credentials after use; mark function as audit-required

tricky_patterns.description: Uses System.DirectoryServices.DirectorySearcher and DirectoryEntry for LDAP queries
tricky_patterns.mitigation: Use ldap3 crate for cross-platform LDAP; windows crate for Windows-specific AD APIs
tricky_patterns.rust_strategy: 1) ldap3::LdapConn for LDAP operations. 2) windows::Win32::NetworkManagement::NetApi32 for AD-specific APIs. 3) Abstract behind trait for testability
tricky_patterns.cross_platform_note: Linux support limited to LDAP protocol; some Windows AD features require native APIs (unavailable on Linux)

tricky_patterns.mitigation: Use wmi crate for Windows; stub/error on Linux
tricky_patterns.cross_platform_note: WMI unavailable on Linux; functions will return NotSupported error

tricky_patterns.description: Uses reflection to introspect objects and print properties: o.GetType().GetMembers()
tricky_patterns.mitigation: Use serde for structured serialization; Debug trait for debugging output
tricky_patterns.rust_strategy: 1) Derive Debug for all types. 2) Implement Display for user-facing output. 3) Use serde_json for structured output option

tricky_patterns.description: Methods return IEnumerable<T> with yield return for lazy evaluation
tricky_patterns.c_sharp_code: foreach (var result in searchResults) { yield return ProcessResult(result); }
tricky_patterns.mitigation: Return Iterator trait or collect into Vec
tricky_patterns.rust_strategy: 1) Return impl Iterator<Item = T> for memory efficiency. 2) Provide .collect() option for Vec<T>. 3) Use streaming where possible
tricky_patterns.performance_note: Iterator trait provides zero-cost lazy evaluation

tricky_patterns.description: Extensive use of nullable types: string (nullable), int?, DateTime?, etc.
tricky_patterns.rust_strategy: 1) string → Option<String>. 2) int? → Option<i32>. 3) Required params → non-Option types. 4) Use #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] for clean JSON

tricky_patterns.description: System.Net.NetworkCredential for username/password; stored in plaintext in memory
tricky_patterns.mitigation: Use secrecy crate to protect credentials in memory; zeroize on drop
tricky_patterns.rust_strategy: 1) Define NetworkCredential struct with SecretString for password. 2) Implement Zeroize trait. 3) Mark password field with #[zeroize(skip)] in serialization. 4) Document that credentials are sensitive

tricky_patterns.description: COM reference to ActiveDs library for ADS_NAME_TYPE_ENUM
tricky_patterns.mitigation: Hard-code enum values from COM type library; use windows crate bindings if available
tricky_patterns.rust_strategy: Define enum with #[repr(u32)] and explicit discriminants matching COM values; no runtime COM dependency needed

tricky_patterns.description: C# uses exceptions for error handling; catch blocks for control flow
tricky_patterns.mitigation: Use Result<T, E> with thiserror for structured errors
tricky_patterns.rust_strategy: 1) Define SharpViewError enum with variants for each error category. 2) Use ? operator for propagation. 3) Implement From<T> for error conversions. 4) Log errors with tracing crate
tricky_patterns.benefit: Explicit error handling, no hidden control flow

tricky_patterns.description: Uses .NET Regex and PCRE.NET library for pattern matching
tricky_patterns.mitigation: Use regex crate (Rust-native) or pcre2 crate for compatibility
tricky_patterns.rust_strategy: Use regex crate by default; test for compatibility with original patterns
tricky_patterns.compatibility_note: Rust regex is not 100% compatible with .NET/PCRE; may need adjustments
